meta.title: UNPLUGGED
meta.subtitle: Forensic mystery
meta.disclaimer: Inspired around d4vd's case, based on Essay #3

intro.text: * Somewhere in the city, a song is still playing on repeat.
* But the artist who made it has not been seen since the news broke.
* The internet has already reached a verdict.
* Terminal access granted. Case 0411-27 is yours, {name}.
* Type <y>help</> for commands. Type <y>list</> to see the files.

n0va.name: N. Vance (n0va)
n0va.bio: The name the internet shouted first. Was in the studio that night.

rex.name: R. Hale
rex.bio: Controls the contracts, the lease and the paperwork.

tessa.name: T. Rowe
tessa.bio: Last person to leave the studio. Works night shifts at a hospital.

objectives.text: Find out who drove the car

deductions.text: * KEY-B belongs to the management valet set. Its only authorised user is R. Hale. He signed it out at 22:55. Whoever drove that car was holding Rex's key.
* n0va badged into Studio A at 19:02 and did not badge out until 03:02. The car moved at 02:09. He was behind a locked door. The man the internet convicted has an alibi.
* The hospital time clock puts Tessa on shift from 22:52 to 07:10. And her last message from Mara was a warning about Rex.

deductions.blocked_text: * The footage looks damning. But a good analyst rules people OUT before ruling one IN. You still have an open suspect.
deductions.text: * The HALEWOOD jacket. The key fob. The face match at the garage exit. While n0va sat at a mixing desk, R. Hale drove the car away.
* 'Stay where you are. Don't talk to anyone.' Motive and intent, in his own voice. It builds the case but doesn't close it.
* The contract change that erased Mara's credit runs through Rex. That's a motive. It's not proof.
* A lawyer, a prepaid phone, a ride from the garage area at 02:58. Suspicious. But none of it places him at the car.
* They argued. That's motive at best. An argument is not a crime, and the chat says nothing about who drove the car.
* Millions of posts. Zero evidence. Popularity is not proof, and a trending hashtag is not a witness.
* The telemetry says KEY-B moved the car. n0va's key is KEY-A. This file doesn't point at him. Find out who holds KEY-B.
* KEY-A is n0va's. But KEY-B is the key that drove the car. Look at who signed THAT one out.
* KEY-B drove the car, yes. But the telemetry doesn't say whose key it is. You need a registry.
* She left the chat at 22:30. A chat doesn't tell you where she went. Is there a statement from her?
* The door audit shows her leaving at 22:30. It doesn't show where she went next.

hints.text_needs: * Think. The telemetry says KEY-B moved the car. Who holds that key? Try <y>search KEY-B</>.
hints.text: * You have the key registry. Who signed out KEY-B? Try <y>submit rex 5</>.

hints.text_needs: * Where was n0va that night? The studio logs who walks through its doors. Try <y>search badge</>.
hints.text: * The door audit shows where n0va was. Does it clear him? Try <y>submit n0va 7</>.
* Tessa left at 22:30. Her interview may say where she went. <y>examine 8</>, then <y>submit tessa 8</>.

hints.text_needs: * One timestamp keeps showing up in the telemetry: 02:09. Try <y>search 02:09</>.
hints.text: * The camera index places someone at the car. Try <y>submit rex 9</>.

Field survey: what college students think

epilogue.text: * CASE CLOSED. The evidence points to <y>R. Hale</>.
* KEY-B. The voicemail. The footage. The paper trail.
* n0va was cleared by a door log. But the internet convicted him in 25 hours.
* That got us thinking about the real world...

epilogue_survey.text: * We asked college students, ages 17 to 23, how they handle this.
* <y>{s:6:1}</> said the SERIOUSNESS of an allegation matters most. Only <y>{s:6:2}</> said strong evidence. And <y>{s:6:3}</> said a court verdict.
* <y>{s:3:2}</> would stop supporting an accused artist, but only until more facts are known.
* <y>{s:5:1}</> said an artist's actions can change the meaning of their songs completely.
* <y>{s:7:1}</> said fans definitely have a responsibility to consider an artist's ethics.
* The song stays the same. The way we hear it might not.
* Evidence first. Opinion second. That's the whole job.
